paper.title: What Spring Security Does
paper.context: Review a fictional Servlet-based Spring MVC application. Apply the stated security and business policies at their own boundaries.

objectives.cross-servlet-boundary: Identify where security runs relative to the controller.
objectives.inspect-evidence: Distinguish verified authentication from authority and permission.
objectives.inspect-protection: Explain how an enabled protection applies to a specific request.
objectives.separate-policy: Keep request-level authority checks and record-level rules distinct.
objectives.review-deployment: Explain how a framework applies a protocol and checks a deployment contract.

questions.prompt: A Servlet authentication filter receives a username and submitted evidence. What should establish the authenticated principal?

choices.alpha: The submitted username if the account exists
choices.beta: A successful result from the configured authentication components
choices.gamma: The existence of an anonymous context

questions.prompt: The route requires hasAuthority("invoice:read"). The verified caller has invoice:view. No authority hierarchy is configured. What follows?

choices.alpha: Verified identity satisfies every guarded route
choices.beta: Matching the invoice prefix grants access
choices.delta: The response must come from the controller

questions.prompt: Which component initially invokes Spring Security’s registered Servlet filter in a standard Servlet deployment?
A controller marker is absent after a configured request guard denies an update. Which interpretation follows from this evidence?

choices.alpha: The controller necessarily threw an exception
choices.beta: The absence proves the controller mapping is missing
choices.gamma: The request must have skipped Spring Security
choices.delta: The downstream MVC handler can be skipped by the filter chain

questions.prompt: A verified browser session has the required route authority. POST has no valid CSRF evidence and default protection applies. Which outcome fits?

choices.beta: The CSRF gate can stop the request before the handler
choices.gamma: GET and POST both require a CSRF token under the default matcher
choices.delta: The service should decide whether CSRF evidence is valid

questions.prompt: A route allows verified invoice readers. Two invoices belong to different accounts. What is the next required input for a record-level decision?

choices.alpha: The stored account for the requested invoice and the caller’s verified scope
choices.gamma: The account name submitted by the client alone
choices.delta: Whether the HTTP transport encrypted the path

questions.prompt: A team migrates from a different HTTP framework to Spring Security. Which part should remain the responsibility of the protocol?

choices.alpha: The sequence of Spring Security filters
choices.beta: Which database field means invoice owner
choices.gamma: The semantics of the HTTP method and response interface

questions.prompt: A sanitized trace shows a non-null AnonymousAuthenticationToken. A reporting method requires a verified user. What should a reviewer conclude?

choices.beta: The route permits access because the token exists
choices.gamma: The reporting service can trust claims in the request body
choices.delta: The trace alone does not establish a verified user

questions.prompt: In the isolated example, what happens when the granted authority is REPORT:READ and the requirement is report:read?

choices.alpha: The decision denies because the exact spelling differs
choices.beta: The decision permits because authority names ignore case
choices.gamma: The decision requires a second AuthenticationManager call
choices.delta: The decision uses the display name instead

questions.prompt: A refactoring retains route policy but removes the check linking reports to the current workspace. Which test specifically detects this regression?

choices.alpha: Send an unauthenticated request to the reporting route
choices.beta: Use a verified report reader requesting a record outside its authorized workspace
choices.gamma: Use a reader and a record from its workspace
choices.delta: Validate that the reporting route still appears in MVC mappings

questions.prompt: Both a rejected CSRF request and a domain refusal give a denial in a test environment. Which trace differentiates the two under the stated design?

choices.gamma: Filter policy decision plus controller and service reachability
choices.delta: A full dump of cookies and credentials

questions.prompt: Describe how to verify a browser export release where authenticated staff need a route authority, a valid POST, and a record within their workspace. Explain which layers run, what evidence each uses, and which failures should reach the controller.

feedback.alpha: Account lookup alone does not verify evidence.
feedback.beta: Verified evidence establishes the returned identity for the configured mechanism.
feedback.gamma: An anonymous token represents an unverified caller.
feedback.delta: A rule declares a requirement without establishing identity.

verified-caller.reason: Inspect the verified Authentication rather than the submitted identifier.

feedback.alpha: Authentication alone does not grant this action.
feedback.beta: The supplied authority name is checked directly.
feedback.gamma: invoice:view is distinct from the exact configured authority.

authority-name.reason: Compare granted and required names exactly, including case.

feedback.alpha: The container dispatches through its mapped filter chain.
feedback.gamma: Business logic runs within application handling.
feedback.delta: An external provider may verify some evidence, but does not invoke the container’s filter.

servlet-owner.reason: Locate the container registration and its Spring delegate during startup review.

feedback.alpha: The marker is consistent with the controller never running.
feedback.beta: The guard can stop before handler lookup.
feedback.delta: A filter can handle or stop the request without invoking downstream processing.

mvc-marker.reason: Use test markers to distinguish route enforcement from MVC execution.

feedback.alpha: Session identity and CSRF validation are independent.
feedback.beta: The default matcher applies to POST.
feedback.gamma: The default excludes safe methods such as GET.
feedback.delta: This fixture provides a filter-level CSRF check.

post-guard.reason: Keep CSRF enabled for the stated browser flow and test the rejected path.

feedback.alpha: That binds the requested record to authoritative ownership.
feedback.beta: It identifies the endpoint, not ownership.
feedback.gamma: Caller input is not authoritative scope.
feedback.delta: TLS does not establish application ownership.

record-policy.reason: Retain resource checks when route authorization succeeds.

feedback.beta: That is domain data and policy.
feedback.gamma: The protocol defines the interface independent of the implementation.
feedback.delta: That choice depends on the configured mechanism.

wire-contract.reason: Use protocol specifications for the wire and the Spring reference for mechanisms.

feedback.beta: Permission depends on policy and trustworthy identity.
feedback.gamma: Those claims do not prove who sent them.
feedback.delta: The anonymous object is infrastructure context.

anonymous-context.reason: Test the actual trust level and policy rather than checking for a non-null object.

feedback.alpha: No normalization or matching role hierarchy is configured in the example.
feedback.beta: The fixture requires the exact string.
feedback.gamma: The decision uses the supplied Authentication.
feedback.delta: Principal display text does not supply a missing authority.

case-sensitive.reason: Treat authority names as a reviewed contract between verification and the guard.

feedback.beta: This passes route authorization and exercises the independent domain denial.
feedback.gamma: That verifies the positive path alone.
feedback.delta: Mapping says nothing about record scope.

locate-regression.reason: Use matched positive and negative domain cases with the same route authority.

feedback.alpha: Different layers can use the same code.
feedback.gamma: The boundary markers tell whether execution entered MVC and the domain.
feedback.delta: Secret material is unnecessary to identify the boundary.

correct-layer.reason: Assert the reached layer with a sanitized test marker.

release-plan.reason: Use Servlet request filters for configured protection, authentication and route authorization. CSRF validation independently protects the POST. The authorization manager evaluates the verified identity and required authority. A rejected filter does not continue to MVC in this fixture. MVC dispatches approved requests, then the service compares verified scope with authoritative record ownership. HTTP defines method and response semantics. Test absent identity, invalid CSRF evidence, missing authority, wrong stored workspace and successful export with redacted boundary markers.
rubric: Separate framework policy from HTTP semantics.
Identify Servlet filtering before MVC for this route.
Distinguish authentication, CSRF and authority evidence.
Use trusted stored record and workspace scope.
Include allowed and denied paths and expected controller reachability.
